Hi all —

I pulled together the technical details below to help your infra/security teams. Also attaching our short VPC guide (redwood_vpc_guide.pdf).

VPC peering / networking
- Redwood will request peering from our infra AWS account: 987654321000.
- For peering we need: Acme VPC ID and Acme AWS account ID.
- Outbound egress: we use a stable prefix list; current egress IPv4 ranges for POC are: 52.24.198.0/24, 34.210.45.0/24, 3.129.76.0/24 (please add these to your allowlist). All communication uses TLS 443.
- Optional: if you prefer private connectivity instead of peering, we can discuss AWS Transit Gateway or PrivateLink (adds time / complexity).

SAML / SSO
- SP details (ACS & entity): ACS URL = https://poc-auth.redwood.ai/saml/acs
  Entity ID = urn:redwood:poc:sp
- We support Okta and Azure AD. If you can share either the metadata URL or the raw XML, we can configure and send a test assertion.

KMS / secrets
- POC options:
  1) Customer-managed KMS: we can be granted decrypt/encrypt via a key policy role; please add role arn:aws:iam::<redwood-account-id>:role/RedwoodKmsAccess (we will supply the exact account id once legal is done).
  2) Redwood-managed keys: we can manage keys for the POC (easier, faster).
- Secrets: we support AWS Secrets Manager and HashiCorp Vault. For POC, Secrets Manager is simplest.

Docs / links
- VPC guide (attached): redwood_vpc_guide.pdf
- MAP template (Marissa's sheet) — please keep edits in the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-ACME-MAP

If Acme can confirm the egress prefixes and Okta metadata, we can schedule the technical kickoff and I’ll walk through the peering steps live.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
